submission.natural_language_explanation: The pole fires on tokens whose referent the text has not pinned down: withheld or unknown identity (unknown, unnamed, unidentified, unspecified, anonymous, secret, hidden, invisible, mysterious, unverified, unreliable), unknown-identity people (stranger, suspect, intruder, attacker, gunman, killer, traitor) and reported or unverified information (rumour, story, message, warning, memory, noticed, confirmed, monitoring, surveillance), with weaker firing on indefinite reference (they, someone, everyone, nobody). It sits at or near zero on concrete, individually identified referents - named people, ordinary objects, body parts, occupations, animals, numbers and everyday physical actions - so it marks an unresolved referent or unverified claim rather than a topic.

adversarial_test_results.prompt:
Every autumn the county fair returns to the same field beside the river, and every autumn the organising committee argues about the same three things: the price of a stall, the noise curfew, and what to do about the old grandstand. This year the argument about the grandstand did not happen. At the October meeting the chair, Douglas Fairbairn, announced that the structure had been condemned in August after an inspection he called thorough, and that the committee had already accepted a quote for its removal. Nobody at the meeting had seen the inspection report. Fairbairn said copies were available on request from the parish office, though the office later said it had received none.

The fair itself went ahead with record attendance. The weather held, the pie contest drew sixty-one entries, and the prize for the largest pumpkin went to a grower from the next valley for the third year running. Livestock numbers were up, the car park filled by nine each morning, and the volunteer rota held together despite two last-minute absences. On Saturday evening the band played forty minutes longer than scheduled because the crowd would not leave, and the committee voted to book them again before the stalls were packed away.

It was the money that undid the goodwill. At the November meeting the treasurer, Priya Nandakumar, presented the accounts and pointed to a payment of eleven thousand pounds to a firm she could not identify in the minutes. Fairbairn said the payment covered the demolition survey and that the firm had asked to stay out of the public record while it tendered for other work in the county. The minutes record the vote but not the name of the contractor. When a reporter for the local paper asked for the invoice, the parish clerk said the request would be considered and then stopped answering emails.

By December the story had travelled further than anyone expected. A former committee member, who would speak only if not named, said the quote had been discussed in a private session in September, weeks before the inspection was supposedly carried out. That claim has not been verified, and the former member declined to provide any document. Another resident said she had heard a rumour that the grandstand had been sold for scrap before the condemnation notice was issued; she could not remember who told her. The county council said it was monitoring the situation but had no comment on the contractor, the quote, or the timing of the inspection.

At the January meeting the committee voted to publish the accounts in full. The published version lists the eleven thousand pounds, a date, and a reference number, and beneath the reference number the words awarded to contractor. No company name appears anywhere in the document. Fairbairn told the meeting that the omission was a clerical error and that the name would be added at the next revision. Nandakumar asked when that revision would be ready. He said he did not know. She asked who had typed the original. He said he could not recall. The meeting moved on to the price of a stall.

Outside, the field was empty and the grandstand was gone, leaving a rectangle of paler grass where it had stood for eighty years. A dog walker stopped at the fence and asked a volunteer what had happened to it. The volunteer said there had been an accident, then corrected herself and said there had been a survey, then said she was not sure and pointed at the office. The office was closed. The sign on the door gave a telephone number and no name.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Places an unnamed contractor, an unchecked claim and a rumour deep inside a passage of roughly six hundred words, testing whether the claimed unresolved-referent feature fires beyond short local contexts as the hypothesis predicts.
